transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… thanks. I guess what brought me in is I’ve been making these kind of careless mistakes at work, and it’s getting hard to brush off.

I supervise a sales team, and on reports I’ll copy the wrong numbers from the dashboard, or I’ll miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check, even when I thought I’d gone back over it. It’s not like I don’t care or I’m trying to rush through it… I mean, I try to be careful. It just keeps happening more than I’d like, and it’s embarrassing. Does that make sense?
Have problems with attention or careless mistakes like this been present since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, but my mom still brings up notes teachers sent home in elementary school.

They’d say I rushed through my work, misplaced or lost homework, talked when I wasn’t supposed to, and had trouble staying in my seat unless somebody reminded me. I guess I kind of hoped I’d grown out of that, but looking back, it was there pretty early.
Do these attention problems also cause trouble outside of work, like at home or in daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it’s mostly just work, but it does spill over.

At work it’s gotten serious enough that my manager actually put it in a formal review, which was… not great. And at home, I think I sometimes tell myself it’s little stuff, but it causes tension because people feel like they can’t really count on me to follow through on things. I don’t mean to put them in that position, but I can see why they get frustrated.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a constant way, at least.

I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, bills, whether I messed something up—but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying about everything for no reason. If anything, it’s usually tied to something specific. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Not really depressed, I don’t think. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, and embarrassed when I drop the ball, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down most of the time or anything like that.

I’m trying to answer that the right way… I just don’t think “depressed” is the word I’d use.
Have you had any recent illness, head injury, or other medical problem around the time these concentration mistakes got worse?

No, not that I can think of. I haven’t had, like, a head injury or some big illness around when this got worse.

I guess I’m not totally sure what would count as a medical problem, but nothing obvious comes to mind.
